crossRefs.note: I wish that you would bear with me in a little foolishness, but indeed you do bear with me.
I speak by way of disparagement, as though we had been weak. Yet in whatever way anyone is bold (I speak in…
For if I would desire to boast, I will not be foolish; for I will speak the truth. But I refrain, so that no man may…
I have become foolish in boasting. You compelled me, for I ought to have been commended by you, for I am in no way…
I wish that you would bear with me in a little foolishness, but indeed you do bear with me.
For you bear with the foolish gladly, being wise.

translations.web: I say again, let no one think me foolish. But if so, yet receive me as foolish, that I also may boast a little.
translations.bsb: I repeat: Let no one take me for a fool. But if you do, then receive me as a fool, so that I too may boast a little.
translations.kjv: I say again, Let ➔ no man think me a fool; if otherwise, yet as a fool receive me, that I may boast myself a little.
translations.asv: I say again, let no man think me foolish; but if ye do, yet as foolish receive me, that I also may glory a little.
